statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, the Gibraltar Registrar issues written grounds under s.37 Companies Act 2014. Procedure: (1) file a revised name re-submission within 14 days at the reduced statutory fee; (2) if re-submission is refused, request internal administrative review by Gibraltar Companies House within 21 days; (3) failing review, apply to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar for judicial review by originating summons (commercial best practice: within 21 days; statutory limit 3 months); (4) concurrently reserve the Bermuda name under s.12 Companies Act 1981, with appeal to the Bermuda Minister of Finance within 30 days of a Bermuda refusal; (5) a third-party opposition received during the 28-day reservation window is adjudicated by the Registry; the applicant may submit written submissions and defend the name at a Registry hearing before final registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. Gibraltar s.61 Companies Act 2014 mandates a physical registered office in Gibraltar for service of process and statutory notices; a virtual office is not acceptable as the sole registered office. Remote day-to-day operations are lawful provided a GFSC-licensed corporate services provider supplies the physical registered office and the company maintains demonstrable substance indicators (Gibraltar resident director or alternate, board meeting minutes held in Gibraltar, accounting records kept in Gibraltar). The Bermuda Exempted Company must also maintain a separate Bermuda registered office under s.67 Companies Act 1981 through a licensed Bermuda CSP; a pure virtual arrangement without either physical office will fail ESR 2019 and Bermuda ESR 2018 substance tests for a geographically mobile social casino publisher.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk within 24 months of incorporation: 35% for a Gibraltar Companies House registry compliance inspection; 20% for a Bermuda Registrar/ESR inspection where the exempted company relies on pure-equity-holding exemption treatment; combined risk rises to 55% if the social casino publishing activity is conducted through the Gibraltar presence without contemporaneous substance evidence (board minutes, employment or outsourcing contracts, IAP revenue accounting records located in Gibraltar).

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow deposit are required under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014; the subscriber may fix the issued share capital at nominal or nil-paid value, and the allotment is recorded in the Statement of Capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS RESOLVED THAT: (1) The subscriber named in the Statement of Capital hereby takes up the total authorised subscription of Ordinary Shares in accordance with the Memorandum and Articles, such shares being credited as fully paid; (2) The registered office be and is hereby established at the address registered in the Statement of Registered Office and the registered agent is appointed; (3) [Name] is appointed Director, [Name] is appointed Principal Officer, and [Name] is appointed Company Secretary, each having consented to act; (4) The officers are jointly and severally authorised to file the incorporation forms, pay the applicable registry fees, open bank accounts and execute post-registration documents; and (5) This resolution is immediately effective and may be certified by the Company Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the company name and screen subscribers

In parallel, verify the identity and address of every natural-person subscriber through a Gibraltar licenced registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as misleading or too similar, promptly file a written objection response and pay the resubmission fee, or submit two alternative names in the same booking; if refusal is based on third-party rights, provide signed consent of the rights holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the constitutional documents before a notary

Memorandum and Articles of Association executed by all subscribers
Statement of Capital and initial shareholding
Consent to act of each director and the company secretary

step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial identity verification fails, supply apostilled or consular-legalised identification and source-of-funds evidence; if a constitutional clause is inconsistent with the Companies Act, amend it by a supplementary assent signed by all subscribers and resubmit to the notary before filing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Bermuda: Registrar of Companies and the Office of the Tax Commissioner (no income tax in force). Gibraltar: HM Government of Gibraltar Main Office, Income Tax Office / Commissioner of Income Tax; portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/tax. If a UK VAT nexus arises: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC); portal: https://www.gov.uk/hmrc.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Bermuda Exempted Company obtains its Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation and, if desired, a Tax Exemption Certificate under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966. If it establishes a branch, agency, place of business or effective management in Gibraltar, the company must be registered with Gibraltar Companies House under the Overseas Companies Regulations, appoint a Gibraltar-resident agent and registered office, and then apply to the Income Tax Office for a Gibraltar Tax Identification Number (TIN). If the company remains entirely managed and controlled from Bermuda and has no Gibraltar permanent establishment, no Gibraltar TIN is required. For UK VAT purposes, where a non-established company makes taxable supplies in the UK (for example through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing), it must apply directly to HMRC for a United Kingdom VAT registration number using the non-established taxable person procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The Bermuda Exempted Company may make the statutory election to be treated as an exempted undertaking under the Bermuda Companies Act and may apply for a Tax Exemption Certificate guaranteeing the absence of Bermuda income tax for up to fifty years. Gibraltar does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime, but the company may elect to be treated as a Gibraltar Qualifying Company if it satisfies statutory substance conditions, or as a non-resident company if central management and control is exercised outside Gibraltar. Hybrid mismatch elections are constrained under the OECD BEPS Action 2 rules as reflected in Gibraltar's Income Tax Act, which disallows any unintended double non-taxation outcome.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar does not impose VAT or GST; indirect taxation is limited to customs and excise duties on physical imports. Digital supplies of simulated social casino and virtual slots games via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing are outside any Gibraltar turnover tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable in Gibraltar because no VAT or GST is in force. If UK VAT applies because the entity is the supplier of record for digital services to UK consumers, HMRC requires compulsory registration regardless of turnover for non-established suppliers; the domestic GBP 85,000 threshold is not a relevant exemption for a non-UK taxable person.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar has no real-time electronic fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mandate for digital services. Invoices may be issued in ordinary commercial form. If the company becomes UK VAT-registered, HMRC Making Tax Digital requires returns to be filed via API-compatible software, but no invoice-level clearance is imposed. Apple and Google transaction receipts, IAP validation records, and payment provider settlement files constitute acceptable electronic fiscal evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Digital services cannot be zero-rated merely because the recipient or download occurs abroad. Under UK VAT rules, B2C digital supplies to UK consumers are standard-rated at 20%; B2B digital supplies to a customer outside the UK are outside the scope or zero-rated where the supplier retains conclusive evidence of the customer's business status and location. Physical goods exported from the UK or Gibraltar to a third-country destination may be zero-rated only when the exporter holds the customs export declaration, transport documentation, and proof of removal from the fiscal territory within the statutory period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document or electronic export declaration) endorsed by HM Customs Gibraltar or HMRC
Commercial invoice and packing list stating the exact value and nature of the goods or digital service in the settlement currency
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR haulier document, or equivalent third-party transport proof evidencing export to a destination outside the fiscal territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice showing transfer of export proceeds to a Gibraltar-licensed EMI bank account within 180 days
For digital services: IP and geolocation evidence, customer VAT registration where applicable, and Apple/Google app-store transaction settlement ledger proving the place of supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating or outside-the-scope treatment is denied ab initio where the mandatory export evidence bundle is incomplete. The tax authority may assess underdeclared VAT retrospectively for four years, extended to twenty years in the case of deliberate error, and impose a civil penalty of up to 100% of the VAT evaded. Where fraudulent documentation is submitted, criminal penalties including imprisonment and unlimited fines may apply under UK VATA 1994 and the Gibraltar Criminal Justice Ordinance; personal liability may extend to directors where the Bermuda Exempted Company is dissolved.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England as monetary-policy anchor for the Gibraltar pound (GIP) under a fixed 1:1 GBP parity; Government of Gibraltar Currency Commission as sole GIP note and coin issuer; Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as statutory banking and AML/CFT supervisor under the Financial Services Act 2019 and Proceeds of Crime Act 2015; Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) as home-state regulator of the Bermuda Exempted Company for Certificate of Exempted Status, Beneficial Ownership, and Economic Substance filings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full unrestricted convertibility without exchange controls. The United Kingdom and Gibraltar impose no current-account or capital-account restrictions; GIP and GBP circulate interchangeably within Gibraltar and USD, EUR, and other major currencies are freely bankable and transferable. Profit remittance (dividends, interest, royalties, management fees) from the Bermuda Exempted Company attracts zero Gibraltar withholding tax and requires no convertibility or remittance permit; the only practical frictions are GFSC-mandated AML/CFT verifications, source-of-funds documentation, and proof that beneficial ownership is transparent across the Bermuda, Gibraltar, and UK sovereignty chain.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender or mandatory repatriation obligations exist. The UK Exchange Control Act 1947 was repealed for both the UK and Gibraltar, and Gibraltar has enacted no successor surrender regime. Export receipts (Apple and Google app-store net settlements, licensing revenues, and content royalties) may be retained in GIP, GBP, USD, EUR, or any freely convertible currency, held onshore or offshore, and applied to intercompany loans or expenses without conversion ratios, registration, or statutory time limits, subject only to general GFSC AML/CFT record-keeping duties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium with legal constraints. A GFSC-licensed Payment Institution or Electronic Money Institution under the Financial Services (Payment Services) Act 2019 is a legal and viable supplementary treasury rail in Gibraltar. However, a foreign (UK FCA-authorised, EU PSD2, or offshore) EMI cannot passport into Gibraltar post-Brexit and must itself obtain GFSC authorisation; in practice most digital-first EMIs (UK or Malta neobanking platforms) reject Bermuda-Exempted-Company clients lacking local Gibraltarian management, a physical office, and a full UBO interview. Recommended architecture: the tier-1 Gibraltar bank remains the principal clearing and liquidity nexus, with a GFSC-licensed EMI added only for segregated low-value inbound app-store settlements and domestic working-capital disbursements; unlicensed or non-passported offshore EMIs should be avoided entirely at this medium-risk-enhanced tier.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandated in practice. GFSC AML/CFT Guidance Notes and prevailing Gibraltar bank KYC policies require a face-to-face identity and conduct interview for at least one director and each beneficial owner when onboarding a non-resident-incorporated client such as a Bermuda Exempted Company. Remote video onboarding is tolerated only by exception for low-risk corporates with a pre-existing GFSC-regulated banker; for this social-casino scope, the interview must be conducted at the Gibraltar branch, at a GFSC-approved affiliated office, or before an acceptable notary public, with original or apostilled corporate documents (certificate of inception, register of directors, UBO declaration, board resolutions) submitted and certified within 90 days of provisional account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Bermuda Exempted Company incorporated outside Gibraltar with an opaque or nominee-bearing ownership topology and no immediate local regulatory footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BMA Certificate of Exempted Status, Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, current Beneficial Ownership Register confirmation, shareholders register and directors register, UBO statutory declarations, notarised board resolutions appointing the Gibraltar registered agent and local management team, and a Gibraltar legal counsel confirmation that no nominee conceals the underlying beneficial owner; the bank's beneficial-ownership attestation form must show the full chain from the Exempted Company to every natural-person UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: social-casino and virtual-slots publishing sector is presumed to carry a gambling nexus, attracting PEP/sanctions-enhanced due diligence and regulatory-licence ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal legal opinion from UK and Gibraltar counsel confirming that simulated social-casino mechanics (no real-money wagers, no cash-out, no prize staking, virtual-currency only) fall outside the Gibraltar Gambling Act 2005 and UK Gambling Act 2005 licensing net; written confirmation from the Government of Gibraltar Gambling Division or GFSC of non-licensability; Apple App Store and Google Play Console compliance certifications; published end-user terms excluding gambling characteristics; 18+ age-gating policy; responsible gaming statement; and a no-real-money audit trail of the virtual-currency flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: high-velocity microtransactions settled through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing create micro-laundering, mule-account, and counterparty-traceability risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Developer/Publisher documents evidencing that Apple and Google act as merchant of record for all consumer payments; official payout schedules reconciling net settlements from Apple and Google (not individual consumers) into the Gibraltar treasury account; chargeback and refund policy documentation; transaction-monitoring framework with velocity rules, daily caps, anomaly thresholds, and FATF-compliant record retention; and the first six months of historical payout statements proving stable counterparty flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: cross-jurisdictional mismatch among Bermuda legal seat, Gibraltar management, and UK sovereign overlay raises uncertainty on tax residence, economic substance, and reporting obligations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gibraltar Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2020 annual return and substance declaration evidencing Gibraltar as the place of strategic management; Gibraltar board-meeting minutes and director attendance records; management employment contracts and Gibraltar payroll records; Bermuda Economic Substance Act 2018 self-assessment confirmation and Permitted Business Certificate; group structure chart covering the full Bermuda-Gibraltar-UK sovereignty chain; and OECD/EU tax good-standing correspondence for all group entities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: shareholders remit capital via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for larger covered transfers) from a BMA-supervised bank to the Gibraltar treasury account under the purpose narrative 'Capital contribution / share premium injection under Bermuda Companies Act 1981'. The bank requires a capitalisation board resolution, certificate of allotment, updated share register, and source-of-wealth letters for every funding shareholder; transfers exceeding GBP 25,000 trigger beneficial-owner attestation (Form-21-equivalent) and full verification of source of funds (audited financials, sale agreements, or inheritance evidence). All inbound wires are sanctioned-list and PEP screened by the GFSC-compliant bank and matched with LEI/GL references where applicable; cash, crypto-asset, and third-party pass-through funding is categorically unacceptable at this tier.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails comprise: (i) SWIFT MT103 for ordinary trade settlements (development studios, marketing agencies, cloud infrastructure such as AWS/GCP, IP-licensing fees, legal and audit fees) executed in GBP via CHAPS and in EUR via SEPA-CR from the Gibraltarian bank settlement positions; (ii) SWIFT MT700 documentary or standby letters of credit issued by Banco Sabadell Gibraltar for single-supplier contracts above GBP 100,000, particularly gaming-content licence acquisitions, with cash cover or collateral parked in a segregated treasury account; (iii) Apple and Google payout rails transferring net proceeds (USD, EUR, or GBP) from app-store merchant-of-record accounts into the Gibraltar operational account through Wire, SEPA, or Fed clearing on fixed payout cycles; and (iv) no cryptocurrency rails, correspondent-omnibus accounts, or unlicensed third-party payment facilitators are permissible under the enhanced-medium-risk profile.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable GBP/USD outright forwards (tenors up to 12 months) quoted by the Gibraltar bank dealing room or a London clearing bank, used to hedge app-store USD settlements into the GBP functional currency
GBP/EUR and EUR/USD FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) aligning staggered Apple and Google net settlements with monthly disbursement cash-flow calendars

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to illiquid emerging-market notional exposures (e.g., BRL, TRY, ZAR, INR) where local in-app store proceeds cannot be delivered, as permitted under GFSC derivative-activity rules

Cross-currency basis swaps (EUR/USD/GBP) for intercompany loan servicing, dividend anticipation, and interest-rate/fx mismatch hedging between the Bermuda parent balance sheet and the Gibraltar operational treasury

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Annual Government Fee for Exempted Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies – Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on 1 January; payable by 31 January annually; pro-rated half-year fee for companies incorporated after 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge if unpaid after 30 days; 50% surcharge after 6 months; administrative strike-off after 12 months of non-payment; 5-year director disqualification for persistent default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies – Economic Substance Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of financial year end; for a 31 December year end, file no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default penalty of USD 597; non-compliance penalty up to USD 10,000; materially false declaration triggers criminal penalties up to USD 50,000 and director prosecution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Register – Annual Confirmation and Event-Driven Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies – Beneficial Ownership Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Register updated and filed within 30 days of every share transfer or ultimate beneficial owner change; annual integrity certificate attested by directors by 31 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update register attracts civil penalty of USD 25,000; knowingly false declaration is a criminal offence punishable by fine up to USD 50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Return for Overseas (Bermuda) Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies – Companies House
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 21 days after each anniversary of the overseas company's Gibraltar registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties escalating from GBP 50 at 1 month to GBP 500 after 6 months; continued default triggers administrative strike-off of the Gibraltar branch and director disqualification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar UBO Register – Annual Confirmation Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Companies House – Beneficial Ownership Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Co-filed with the annual return; confirmation due within 21 days of the annual return date; any change in beneficial ownership filed within 14 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalties up to GBP 50,000; restriction orders suspending voting and dividend rights; personal director liability for continued breach

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 30 November following the end of the year of assessment for a 31 December basis period; interim instalment payments due 30 April and 30 October
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalty of GBP 100 plus daily penalty of GBP 10 per day up to GBP 1,800; tax-geared penalty up to 20% of the underpaid liability; prolonged default results in criminal summons and seizure of assets

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private Bermuda exempted company is exempt from compulsory statutory audit unless listed, licensed under the banking, insurance, or fund regime, or voluntarily files accounts with the Bermuda Registrar. Gibraltar audit exemption applies where turnover does not exceed GBP 10.2 million, balance-sheet total does not exceed GBP 5.1 million, and average headcount does not exceed 50. A social-casino software publishing holding entity that is unlisted and unregulated is not compulsorily audited in either Bermuda or Gibraltar.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Bermuda permits IFRS, US GAAP, or other acceptable equivalent standards for exempted companies; Gibraltar requires IFRS for all reporting entities with UK GAAP (FRS 102) available for small entities; consolidated group reporting applies IFRS 8 segment disclosure for the Apple IAP and Google Play Billing distribution channels.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Bermuda exempted company must keep a beneficial ownership register at its registered office and file a confirmation with the Bermuda Registrar within 30 days of any transfer of shares or any change to an ultimate beneficial owner; an annual year-end attestation is executed by the directors. In Gibraltar, the UBO particulars must be verified annually and deposited with the Companies House alongside the annual return within 21 days of the return date; any shareholder change must be notified within 14 days. Both registers are maintained in parallel; the Bermuda record prevails for ownership rights and the Gibraltar record governs local disclosure and penalty exposure.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – 3,500 per year for joint Bermuda and Gibraltar registered-office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – 8,000 per year if an audit is voluntarily procured; not statutorily mandated for this entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% Gibraltar corporation tax on chargeable profits accruing in or derived from Gibraltar; 0% Bermuda exempted company tax rate where the entity is not Gibraltar tax-resident (post-2025 Bermuda CIT deferred below the €750m MNE threshold; composite exposure 0%–12.5%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Bermuda Tax Exemption Certificate: statutory assurance of no Bermuda income/PRC tax until statutory expiry (CIT commencement 1 Jan 2025 applies only to large MNE groups ≥ €750m consolidated revenue, not to the simulated startup); Gibraltar Qualifying Companies/AIM? No — Gibraltar does not grant patent-box or gaming incentives; Gross receipts duty? Actually Gibraltar's old
